claims.claim: Enable 802.11r FT (over-the-air or over-DS) with correct mobility domain and key holders so voice clients roam fast.
claims.note: Frontmatter description scope; the fetched page never mentions 802.11r operation, mobility domains, key holders or roaming speed - its only 802.11r references are the inactive task-group label 'TGr - Fast BSS Transition (FT)' and a trademark disclaimer.

claims.claim: FT precomputes keys so a roam skips a full 802.1X exchange.
claims.note: The page is a working-group landing page (sessions, ballots, task-group and document links); it never mentions key precomputation, roaming or 802.1X.

claims.claim: Requires a shared mobility domain ID and key hierarchy across APs on the same SSID (controller or cluster handles it).
claims.note: No occurrence of 'mobility domain', 'key hierarchy', 'SSID' or controller/cluster key sharing anywhere on the page.

claims.claim: Modes: over-the-air (client talks to target AP directly) and over-DS (via the current AP).
claims.note: The page never uses the terms 'over-the-air' or 'over-DS' and describes no FT mechanisms; 'Fast BSS Transition (FT)' appears only as the inactive task-group link label 'TGr'.
The page contains no compatibility comparison of FT modes; 'Over-the-air' appears nowhere in its text.

claims.claim: Some older clients fail to associate to FT-enabled SSIDs
claims.note: No statement about client association failures on FT-enabled SSIDs; the page only lists task groups, ballots and meetings.

claims.claim: "FT adaptive" or mixed modes exist on some platforms
claims.note: The page never mentions 'FT adaptive', mixed FT modes, or any vendor platforms or products.

claims.claim: Test device classes, especially IoT and printers.
claims.note: No mention of IoT devices, printers or per-device-class client testing anywhere on the page.

claims.claim: Alternatives when FT is unsuitable: OKC/PMK caching (vendor-specific, non-standard) or sticky roam avoidance.
claims.note: The page never mentions OKC, PMK caching, sticky clients or roam avoidance; 'PMF' on the page is Protected Management Frames, not PMK.

claims.claim: Capture shows Reassociation Request with FT elements and no full EAP exchange.
claims.note: Verify-section criterion; the page mentions no Reassociation Request, FT elements, EAP or packet capture.

claims.claim: A voice call holds through a walk test with sub-50-ms gaps
claims.note: Verify-section criterion carrying the skill's only number; the page has no voice-call or walk-test guidance and no 50 ms figure - its numbers are meeting dates, ballot IDs and publication dates.

coverage: I took the frontmatter description and every sentence of the body bullets and Verify checklist as claims, splitting the compound lines (client association failures vs FT-adaptive/mixed modes, and the two mode definitions) so that every behaviour, mode name, alternative (OKC/PMK caching, sticky roam avoidance) and the one number (sub-50-ms gaps) is covered; the skill contains no commands, flags or settings. The single listed source was fetched and read, and each claim was checked against it.
